matches.title: Hibernian vs Malisheva
matches.description: Watch Hibernian vs Malisheva highlights and goals from UEFA Europa Conference League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on July 30, 2026. On July 30, 2026 , Hibernian hosted Malisheva in a crucial UEFA Europa Conference League encounter. Both sides entered the pitch with high ambitions, looking to make their mark on the European stage in a match filled with tactical intrigue. A Blistering Opening Half Hibernian started the match with intent, establishing dominance early on and leaving the visitors struggling to find their rhythm. The deadlock was broken in the 9th minute when Owen Elding found the back of the net, courtesy of a well-timed assist from Martin Boyle . The momentum stayed firmly with the hosts as Felix Passlack doubled the lead in the 15th minute after being set up by Nathan Lowe . The clinical nature of the Scottish side’s attack was evident as they exploited gaps in the Malisheva defense. The pressure continued to mount, and by the 35th minute, the result seemed all but certain. Nathan Lowe turned from provider to scorer, converting a chance created by Owen Elding to make it 3-0. While the first half saw some disciplinary issues with yellow cards for Martin Boyle and Josh Mulligan , the tactical superiority of the home side was the defining story heading into the interval. Second Half Control and Late Response As the second half got underway, Hibernian refused to take their foot off the gas. In the 57th minute, Martin Boyle added a fourth goal, further cementing his influence on the game. With a comfortable lead established, several substitutions followed, including the introduction of Chris Cadden and Joe Newell to manage the game's closing stages. Malisheva also looked to their bench for inspiration, bringing on Omer Bajraktari and Krenar Dulaj . Those changes bore fruit for the visitors in the 83rd minute when Omer Bajraktari pulled one back for Malisheva , assisted by Krenar Dulaj . The final moments of the match saw an increase in physical play, leading to bookings for Thibault Klidje , Valmir Nafiu , and Dreni Kryeziou . Despite the late consolation from the away side, the referee's final whistle confirmed a comprehensive performance from Hibernian , who secured a vital result in front of their home crowd.
